title: Values
summary: Functions and constants, typed by TypeScript, inferred results included.

title: Interfaces
summary: An interface is a record; optional, nullable and promised values keep their meaning.

title: Unions
summary: Tagged unions, literal unions and primitive unions each have a ReScript form.

title: Generics
summary: Type parameters become type variables, on types and on functions.

title: Classes
summary: A class is a module with a type, a constructor and its static members.

title: Classes in unions
summary: A class is told apart with instanceof, so a union of classes is a variant.

title: Objects in unions
summary: Plain objects are told apart by their fields, so a union of them is a variant.

title: Shared tags
summary: Members that share a tag are cases of one tagged variant, told apart by their other fields.

title: A whole module
summary: module Api = %ts(...) imports every export; type t = %ts("...#Name") imports one type.

title: Computed types
summary: Utility, mapped and inferred types arrive already evaluated.

title: A package
summary: Module specifiers resolve the way TypeScript resolves them.

title: Only what is imported is checked
summary: One function out of a module of sixty-two, one of which does not even type check.

title: A type error
summary: Using an import wrongly is an ordinary ReScript error.

title: What does not fit
summary: Overloads, any, constraints, untagged object unions: imported, with a note.

title: Two declarations of one class
summary: Each package declares Element. A value of one is accepted where the other is expected.

title: Records and enums already cross
summary: An options object and an enum go from one declaration to another with :>.

title: Cases from two packages
summary: The subclass is tested first, although the two cases are declared in different packages.

title: Converting through a variant
summary: The way from one declaration of Element to another before this change: a test that cannot fail.

title: Coercion between declarations
summary: The same class both ways, a subclass to an ancestor, and inside other types.

title: Where the coercion is implicit
summary: Arguments, record fields and constructor payloads take a class type of another declaration.

title: Where it stays written
summary: The two branches have two types, and neither is the expected one.
expected: This error is what the example shows: the branches of a conditional are not a site that declares a type, so one of them needs a written coercion.

title: A declaration without its superclass
summary: The error names both classes and the superclasses the source declares.
expected: This error is what the example shows: Forms.input does not declare that its class extends Element.
